cards.q: A company makes forecasts each quarter to decide how to optimize operations to meet expected demand. The company uses ML models to make these forecasts. An AI practitioner is writing a report about the trained ML models to provide transparency and explainability to company stakeholders. What should the AI practitioner include in the report?
cards.explanation: Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs) show how a model's predictions change as a single input feature changes, holding all other features constant. They are a standard explainability tool for ML models, especially tree-based ones. For a transparency report, PDPs help stakeholders see which features drive predictions and how. Code, raw training data, or convergence tables don't address explainability, they're internal training artifacts.
tricks: 'transparency / explainability report' + 'tabular ML' = PDP, SHAP values, or feature importance plots

cards.q: A company wants to use language models to create an application for inference on edge devices. The inference must have the lowest latency possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.a: Deploy optimized small language models (SLMs) on edge devices.
options: Deploy optimized small language models (SLMs) on edge devices.
Deploy optimized large language models (LLMs) on edge devices.
Incorporate a centralized small language model (SLM) API for asynchronous communication with edge devices.
Incorporate a centralized large language model (LLM) API for asynchronous communication with edge devices.
cards.explanation: Edge devices have constrained CPU, memory, and intermittent network. Two requirements force the answer: 'inference on edge' rules out cloud APIs (network round-trip = high latency), and 'lowest latency possible' rules out async / centralized calls. SLMs are designed to run on-device with a fraction of the memory of LLMs.
trap: An LLM is too big to deploy on most edge devices. Pick SLM when the question mentions edge.
Centralized API + asynchronous = network latency + queueing = NOT lowest latency.
tricks: 'inference on edge with lowest latency' = small model deployed on the device, never a centralized API

cards.q: A company is developing a mobile ML app that uses a phone's camera to diagnose and treat insect bites. The company wants to train an image classification model by using a diverse dataset of insect bite photos from different genders, ethnicities, and geographic locations. Which principle of responsible AI does the company demonstrate?
cards.explanation: Fairness in responsible AI is about equal performance across demographic groups (gender, ethnicity, geography, age). Diverse training data is a prerequisite for fairness because if your data is skewed toward one group, the model will perform worse for under-represented groups. Other principles: Explainability = can you understand the model's decisions. Governance = controls and policies. Transparency = clarity about how the system works. The diverse-dataset signal in the question maps cleanly to fairness, not the other 3.

cards.q: A company is developing an ML model to make loan approvals. The company must implement a solution to detect bias in the model. The company must also be able to explain the model's predictions. Which solution will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify is the AWS service for both bias detection (pre-training, post-training, in production) and model explainability (using SHAP values to explain individual predictions). For loan approvals, you need both: detect demographic bias in the training data and the predictions, AND explain why each individual loan was approved or denied.
tricks: 'detect bias + explain predictions' = SageMaker Clarify. Data Wrangler = data prep. Model Cards = documentation. AI Service Cards = AWS-published cards for AWS AI services (Rekognition, Polly, etc.)

cards.q: A company has developed a generative text summarization model by using Amazon Bedrock. The company will use Amazon Bedrock automatic model evaluation capabilities. Which metric should the company use to evaluate the accuracy of the model?
options: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) score
cards.explanation: BERTScore measures semantic similarity between generated text and reference text using BERT embeddings, perfect for evaluating summarization where the wording can vary but the meaning must match. F1 = classification metric (precision and recall). AUC = binary classifier ranking quality. RWK = not a standard metric. Bedrock automatic model evaluation supports BERTScore for summarization, ROUGE for summarization comparing n-grams, and BLEU for translation.
tricks: 'evaluate summarization in Bedrock' = BERTScore (or ROUGE)

cards.q: An AI practitioner wants to predict the classification of flowers based on petal length, petal width, sepal length, and sepal width. Which algorithm meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: K-NN is the classic supervised classification algorithm: given a labeled dataset (Iris is the textbook example), classify a new point based on the labels of its nearest neighbors in feature space. K-means is unsupervised clustering. ARIMA is for time-series forecasting. Linear regression predicts a continuous value, not a class.
tricks: 'classify based on similar examples' or 'small labeled dataset, simple classification' = k-NN

cards.q: A company is using custom models in Amazon Bedrock for a generative AI application. The company wants to use a company managed encryption key to encrypt the model artifacts. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS KMS is the canonical service for encrypting data at rest with customer-managed keys (CMK) in nearly every AWS service that supports encryption, including Bedrock custom models. Inspector = vulnerability scanning. Macie = PII discovery in S3. Secrets Manager = secrets/credentials, not encryption keys for model artifacts.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'company-managed encryption key' or 'CMK' = KMS, always

cards.q: A company wants to use large language models (LLMs) to produce code from natural language code comments. Which LLM feature meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Producing code from natural language comments is a classic text generation task: input is a prompt (the comment), output is new text (the code). Text completion is similar but typically shorter (autocomplete). Summarization compresses existing text. Classification assigns labels. Code generation is the flagship LLM use case (Amazon Q Developer, GitHub Copilot, etc.).

cards.q: A company is introducing a mobile app that helps users learn foreign languages. The app makes text more coherent by calling an LLM. The company wants the LLM output to resemble provided examples. Which metric should the company use?
cards.a: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) score
options: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) score
cards.explanation: ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) measures how much of the reference text is captured by the generated text using n-gram overlap. It is the standard metric when you want generated output to resemble provided reference examples (summarization, translation). Loss function value = training metric, not output similarity. Semantic robustness = stability under input perturbation. Latency = speed, not similarity.
tricks: 'output should resemble reference examples' = ROUGE

cards.q: A company notices that its foundation model (FM) generates images that are unrelated to the prompts. The company wants to modify the prompt techniques to decrease unrelated images. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Negative prompts tell a model what to AVOID generating ('do not include flowers', 'no text in the image'). They are widely used in image generation (Stable Diffusion, Bedrock image models) to push outputs away from unwanted concepts. Zero-shot = no examples. Positive prompts = describe what you want (already implied here). Ambiguous prompts = the opposite of what you want.
tricks: 'reduce unrelated/unwanted output' = negative prompts

cards.q: A company wants to use an LLM to generate concise, feature-specific descriptions for the company's products. Which prompt engineering technique meets these requirements?
cards.a: Create prompts for each product category that highlight the key features. Include the desired output format and length.
options: Create one prompt that covers all products. Edit responses to be more specific.
Create prompts for each product category that highlight the key features. Include the desired output format and length.
Include a diverse range of product features in each prompt to generate creative descriptions.
Provide detailed, product-specific prompts to ensure precise descriptions.
cards.explanation: Best practice in prompt engineering: give the model context (product category, key features), specify output format (bullet points, sentences), and length (max words). One generic prompt for all products produces generic output. 'Diverse range of features in each prompt' adds noise. 'Detailed product-specific prompts' is closer but lacks the structure (format + length). The right answer combines specificity (per category) with output structure.

cards.q: A company is developing an ML model to predict customer churn. The model performs well on the training dataset but does not accurately predict churn for new data. Which solution will resolve this issue?
cards.a: Increase the regularization parameter to decrease model complexity.
options: Decrease the regularization parameter to increase model complexity.
Increase the regularization parameter to decrease model complexity.
Add more features to the input data.
Train the model for more epochs.
cards.explanation: Performs well on training, fails on new data = overfitting. Solutions: more regularization (penalize complexity, the right answer), dropout, simpler model, more training data. Decreasing regularization makes overfitting WORSE. Adding features makes overfitting WORSE. Training more epochs makes overfitting WORSE.
trap: More features = MORE overfitting risk, not less.
More epochs = MORE overfitting risk, not less.
Decreasing regularization = MORE complexity = MORE overfitting.
tricks: 'memorizes training, fails on new data' = overfitting -> increase regularization

cards.q: A company wants to build an ML model by using Amazon SageMaker. The company needs to share and manage variables for model development across multiple teams. Which SageMaker feature meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: SageMaker Feature Store is a centralized repository for ML features (variables) with versioning, lineage, and online + offline access. It is the dedicated AWS service for sharing and managing features across teams and models. Data Wrangler = data prep UI. Clarify = bias and explainability. Model Cards = model documentation.
tricks: 'share and manage variables/features across teams' = Feature Store

cards.q: A company is implementing intelligent agents to provide conversational search experiences. The company needs a database service that supports storage and queries of embeddings as vectors. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: Vector embeddings store and similarity search are required for RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) and semantic search. Among the listed options, Aurora PostgreSQL supports the pgvector extension for native vector storage and similarity queries. Athena = SQL on S3 (no vector queries). Redshift = data warehouse (limited vector support). EMR = Spark/Hadoop, not a database. AWS also offers OpenSearch and DocumentDB with vector capabilities, but in this question's choices, Aurora PostgreSQL is the answer.

cards.q: A financial institution is building an AI solution to make loan approval decisions by using a foundation model (FM). The company needs the AI solution's decisions to be explainable. Which factor relates to the explainability?
cards.explanation: Model complexity is the inverse of explainability: simpler models (linear regression, decision trees) are easier to explain than complex ones (deep neural networks, large foundation models). For loan approvals where regulators demand explanations, you trade off some accuracy for explainability by choosing simpler models. Training time, hyperparameter count, and deployment time don't directly relate to explainability.
tricks: 'explainability' factor = model complexity

cards.q: A pharmaceutical company wants to analyze user reviews of new medications and provide a concise overview for each medication. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Create medication review summaries by using Amazon Bedrock LLMs.
options: Create a time-series forecasting model by using Amazon Personalize.
Create medication review summaries by using Amazon Bedrock LLMs.
Create a classification model by using Amazon SageMaker.
Create medication review summaries by using Amazon Rekognition.
cards.explanation: Concise overview of free-text reviews = summarization, a flagship LLM use case. Bedrock provides foundation models that can summarize text. Personalize = recommendation engine. SageMaker classification = label, not summarize. Rekognition = images and video, not text.
tricks: 'summarize free text' = LLM via Bedrock (or Comprehend for simpler key-phrase extraction)

cards.q: A company wants to build a lead prioritization application. The application must give employees the ability to view and adjust the weights assigned to different variables. Which ML model type meets these requirements?
options: Deep learning model built on principal components
cards.explanation: Logistic regression is a linear model whose weights (coefficients) are interpretable: each variable has an explicit weight that you can see and adjust. Deep learning, k-NN, and neural networks have weights that are not human-interpretable in the same way.
tricks: 'view and adjust weights of variables' = logistic regression (or linear regression for continuous output). Lead prioritization = binary classification = logistic regression fits

cards.q: Which strategy will determine if a foundation model (FM) effectively meets business objectives?
cards.a: Assess the model's alignment with specific use cases.
options: Evaluate the model's performance on benchmark datasets.
Analyze the model's architecture and hyperparameters.
Assess the model's alignment with specific use cases.
Measure the computational resources required for model deployment.
cards.explanation: Effectiveness against business objectives requires evaluating the model on YOUR specific use cases, not generic benchmarks. Benchmark scores tell you how the model compares to others on standard tasks. Architecture and hyperparameters are technical details. Compute resources are about cost. Only 'alignment with specific use cases' addresses business objectives.
tricks: 'meets business objectives' = evaluate on use-case-specific data

cards.q: A company needs to train an ML model to classify images of different types of animals. The company has a large dataset of labeled images and will not label more data. Which type of learning should the company use?
cards.explanation: Labeled images = supervised learning. The labels are the ground truth that teaches the model. Unsupervised learning works on UNLABELED data (clustering, dimensionality reduction). Reinforcement learning learns from rewards in an environment. Active learning = the model picks which examples to label next, but the company explicitly will not label more.
tricks: 'large labeled dataset, no more labeling' = supervised learning

cards.q: Which phase of the ML lifecycle determines compliance and regulatory requirements?
cards.explanation: The ML lifecycle (CRISP-DM-style) starts with Business Goal Identification: what are we trying to achieve, what are the success metrics, what regulatory and compliance constraints apply (GDPR, HIPAA, fairness laws). Compliance requirements MUST be defined before any data collection or modeling, because they constrain what data you can use and how. Feature engineering, training, and data collection happen later.
tricks: 'compliance and regulatory requirements' = first phase, business goal identification

cards.q: A food service company wants to develop an ML model to help decrease daily food waste and increase sales revenue. The company needs to continuously improve the model's accuracy. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Use Amazon SageMaker and iterate with newer data.
options: Use Amazon SageMaker and iterate with newer data.
Use Amazon Personalize and iterate with historical data.
Use Amazon CloudWatch to analyze customer orders.
Use Amazon Rekognition to optimize the model.
cards.explanation: Continuous improvement of ML model accuracy = retrain regularly with newer data using a flexible ML platform. SageMaker is the AWS platform for full ML lifecycle (build, train, deploy, monitor, retrain). Personalize = pre-built recommendation engine, not for arbitrary forecasting. CloudWatch = monitoring, not ML. Rekognition = images, irrelevant.
tricks: 'continuously improve a custom ML model' = SageMaker

cards.q: A company has developed an ML model to predict real estate sale prices. The company wants to deploy the model without managing servers or infrastructure. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Deploy by using an Amazon SageMaker endpoint.
options: Deploy on an Amazon EC2 instance.
Deploy on an Amazon EKS cluster.
Deploy by using Amazon CloudFront with Amazon S3.
Deploy by using an Amazon SageMaker endpoint.
cards.explanation: SageMaker endpoints are fully managed, serverless model hosting: AWS provisions the compute, load balancing, scaling, and monitoring. EC2 = manage your own servers. EKS cluster = manage Kubernetes. CloudFront + S3 = static content, not ML inference.
tricks: 'deploy ML model without managing servers' = SageMaker endpoint

cards.q: A company wants to use generative AI to increase developer productivity. What can Amazon Q Developer do?
cards.a: Create software snippets, reference tracking, and open source license tracking.
options: Create software snippets, reference tracking, and open source license tracking.
Run an application without provisioning or managing servers.
Enable voice commands for coding and providing natural language search.
Convert audio files to text documents by using ML models.
cards.explanation: Amazon Q Developer (formerly CodeWhisperer) is the AI coding assistant: real-time code suggestions, reference tracking (when generated code is similar to training code), open source license tracking, security scans. The other choices describe Lambda (serverless app), Polly/Lex/Transcribe (voice), and Transcribe (audio-to-text).
tricks: 'developer productivity AI assistant for code' = Amazon Q Developer

cards.q: A company wants to develop an AI application to help employees check open customer claims, identify details, and access documents. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases.
options: Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Fraud Detector.
Use Agents for Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases.
Use Amazon Personalize with Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases.
Use Amazon SageMaker to train a new ML model.
cards.explanation: Bedrock Agents orchestrate multi-step tasks (look up a claim, fetch documents, summarize) by calling APIs and tools. Bedrock Knowledge Bases ground the LLM in your private data (claims, documents) via RAG. Combined: the agent reasons, the knowledge base provides the data. Fraud Detector = different service. Personalize = recommendation engine. SageMaker training = build a custom model from scratch (slower, more expensive).
tricks: 'AI assistant that takes action and accesses internal docs' = Bedrock Agents + Knowledge Bases

cards.q: A manufacturing company uses AI to inspect products and find damages or defects. Which type of AI application is the company using?
cards.explanation: Inspecting products visually for defects = computer vision, the AI subdomain dealing with images and video. Recommendation system = suggest items to users. NLP = text and language. Image processing is a broader, often non-ML term (photoshop-style operations like resize, filter), while computer vision implies AI/ML on images.
tricks: 'AI inspection of images for defects/anomalies' = computer vision

cards.q: A company wants to create an ML model to predict customer satisfaction. The company needs fully automated model tuning. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: SageMaker is the AWS end-to-end ML platform with built-in Automatic Model Tuning (a.k.a. Hyperparameter Optimization) that uses Bayesian search or random search to find the best hyperparameters for a model. Personalize = pre-built recommendations service, not custom ML. Athena = SQL on S3, no ML training. Comprehend = pre-built NLP, not custom.
tricks: 'fully automated model tuning' = SageMaker (Automatic Model Tuning / HPO)

cards.q: Which technique can a company use to lower bias and toxicity in generative AI applications during the post-processing ML lifecycle?
cards.explanation: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) means a human reviews and validates AI outputs after generation, the canonical post-processing technique to catch bias and toxicity that the model produced. Data augmentation, feature engineering, and adversarial training all happen BEFORE or DURING training, not in post-processing. Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth and Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) are the AWS services that implement HITL.
tricks: 'reduce bias/toxicity AT POST-PROCESSING' = human-in-the-loop

cards.q: A bank has fine-tuned an LLM for loan approvals. The model approves loans faster for a specific demographic. How should the bank fix this MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: Include more diverse training data. Fine-tune the model again.
options: Include more diverse training data. Fine-tune the model again.
Use RAG with the fine-tuned model.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor checks to eliminate bias.
Pre-train a new LLM with more diverse training data.
cards.explanation: The bias comes from skewed training data. Fine-tuning again on more diverse data is the cheapest fix because fine-tuning reuses the existing model weights (small training cost). RAG would let the model retrieve external info but won't change its biased decisions. Trusted Advisor is for AWS infra checks, not ML bias. Pre-training a NEW LLM from scratch costs millions and is not 'most cost-effective'.
tricks: 'fix bias in fine-tuned model cost-effectively' = fine-tune again with more diverse data

cards.q: A company needs to log all requests made to its Amazon Bedrock API. The company must retain the logs securely for 5 years at the lowest possible cost. Which combination meets these requirements? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: CloudTrail logs every API call to AWS services including Bedrock (who called what, when, with what parameters). Logs delivered to S3. For 5-year retention at lowest cost, S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves rarely accessed logs to cheaper tiers without retrieval fees, ideal for unpredictable access. CloudWatch = expensive for long-term logs. Audit Manager = compliance reports, not raw API logs. S3 Standard = pricier than Intelligent-Tiering for old data.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'log API calls + cheap long-term storage' = CloudTrail + S3 Intelligent-Tiering

cards.q: An ecommerce company wants to improve search engine recommendations by customizing results for each user. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Personalize is the AWS managed recommendation engine, purpose-built for personalized rankings, related items, and user-segment targeting. Kendra = enterprise search (relevance, not personalization per user). Rekognition = images and video. Transcribe = speech-to-text.
tricks: 'personalized recommendations per user' = Amazon Personalize

cards.q: A hospital is developing an AI system to assist doctors in diagnosing diseases. Sensitive patient data must not leave the country. Which data governance strategy will ensure compliance?
cards.explanation: Data residency is the requirement that data stays within a specific country or region for legal/compliance reasons (GDPR for EU, HIPAA + state laws for US healthcare, RGPD for France, etc.). Choose AWS Region in the right country and use guardrails (SCPs, Region restrictions) to prevent data leaving. Data quality = accuracy and completeness, unrelated. Data discoverability = catalog. Data enrichment = adding fields.
tricks: 'data must not leave the country' = data residency

cards.q: A company needs to monitor the performance of its ML systems by using a highly scalable AWS service. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: CloudWatch is the AWS service for monitoring metrics, logs, and alarms across all services including ML systems. Trigger words: 'monitor performance' + 'highly scalable AWS service' = CloudWatch. CloudTrail = API audit logs. Trusted Advisor = best-practice checks (not real-time monitoring). Config = configuration history.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'monitor performance and metrics' = CloudWatch

cards.q: A financial institution is using Amazon Bedrock. The VPC is not allowed access to any internet traffic. Which AWS service or feature will meet these requirements?
cards.explanation: PrivateLink creates a private endpoint inside your VPC so traffic to AWS services (including Bedrock) stays on the AWS backbone and never traverses the public internet. Macie = PII detection in S3. CloudFront = CDN, the opposite of private. Internet gateway = the opposite of what's required (it ENABLES internet traffic).
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'access AWS service from VPC without internet' = PrivateLink (or VPC endpoint, same idea)

cards.q: An AI practitioner adds 'show its work by explaining reasoning step by step' to a prompt. Which prompt engineering technique is this?
cards.explanation: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting asks the model to 'think step by step' or 'show its reasoning' before giving the final answer. This consistently improves accuracy on complex tasks (math, multi-step reasoning, code). Prompt injection = security attack to bypass system instructions. Few-shot = give examples in the prompt. Prompt templating = reusable prompt structures.
tricks: 'show reasoning step by step' = chain-of-thought

cards.q: Which AWS service makes foundation models (FMs) available to help users build and scale generative AI applications?
cards.explanation: Bedrock is the AWS service that provides managed access to foundation models from multiple providers (Anthropic, Meta, Amazon Nova, Cohere, AI21, Mistral, Stability AI) via a single API. Q Developer = AI coding assistant. Kendra = enterprise search. Comprehend = pre-built NLP.
tricks: 'access foundation models / build GenAI apps on AWS' = Bedrock

cards.q: A company is building a mobile app for users with visual impairment. The app must hear what users say and provide voice responses. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Use a deep learning neural network to perform speech recognition.
options: Use a deep learning neural network to perform speech recognition.
Build ML models to search for patterns in numeric data.
Use generative AI summarization to generate human-like text.
Build custom models for image classification and recognition.
cards.explanation: Hearing what users say + voice responses requires speech recognition (speech-to-text, e.g. Amazon Transcribe) and speech synthesis (text-to-speech, e.g. Amazon Polly), both built on deep learning neural networks. Pattern search in numeric data = different problem. Generative AI summarization = different problem. Image classification = different problem.
tricks: 'voice input/output' = deep learning speech models (Transcribe + Polly)

cards.q: A company wants to enhance LLM response quality for complex problem-solving tasks requiring detailed reasoning and step-by-step explanations. Which prompt engineering technique meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Same answer pattern as aif-034 but reinforced for emphasis. Chain-of-thought prompting is the technique for complex problem-solving tasks requiring step-by-step reasoning. Few-shot = give examples. Zero-shot = no examples. Directional stimulus prompting = guide the model with hints (less common).
tricks: 'detailed reasoning + step-by-step explanations' = chain-of-thought

cards.q: A company wants to keep its foundation model (FM) relevant by using the most recent data with regular updates. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Continuous pre-training extends a foundation model's knowledge with new domain data on a recurring schedule, keeping it relevant as the world changes. Batch learning = static training on a fixed dataset. Static training = same idea, no updates. Latent training = not a real term. Bedrock supports continuous pre-training of custom models.
tricks: 'keep FM relevant with recent data, regular updates' = continuous pre-training

cards.q: Which option is a characteristic of AI governance frameworks for building trust and deploying human-centered AI technologies?
cards.a: Developing policies and guidelines for data, transparency, responsible AI, and compliance
options: Expanding initiatives across business units to create long-term value
Ensuring alignment with business standards and revenue goals
Overcoming challenges to drive business transformation
Developing policies and guidelines for data, transparency, responsible AI, and compliance
cards.explanation: AI governance is fundamentally about policies and guidelines (data handling, transparency, responsible AI principles, regulatory compliance). The other options describe business-level concerns (initiatives, alignment with revenue, transformation challenges) that are not the core of governance frameworks.
tricks: 'AI governance for trust' = policies + transparency + compliance

cards.q: An ecommerce company is using a generative AI chatbot. The company wants to measure the financial effect of the chatbot. Which metric should it use?
cards.explanation: Financial effect = $ per business unit. Cost per customer conversation gives you a direct unit economic that you can compare to the cost of a human agent and the value generated. Number of inquiries handled = volume, not financial. Cost of training the model = one-time investment, not ongoing financial effect. AHT = operational metric, not financial.
tricks: 'measure financial effect of chatbot' = cost per conversation

cards.q: A company wants to find groups for its customers based on demographics and buying patterns. Which algorithm should the company use?
cards.explanation: Find groups in unlabeled data = clustering = K-means (the default unsupervised clustering algo). K-NN = supervised classification. Decision tree = supervised classification or regression. SVM = supervised classification. The question implies no labels (no 'low-value customer' label exists, you want the algo to discover groups), so the answer is the only unsupervised one: K-means.
tricks: 'find groups / clustering / segments' = K-means

cards.q: A company's LLM is experiencing hallucinations. How can the company decrease hallucinations?
cards.a: Decrease the temperature inference parameter for the model.
options: Set up Agents for Amazon Bedrock to supervise model training.
Use data pre-processing and remove data that causes hallucinations.
Decrease the temperature inference parameter for the model.
Use a foundation model (FM) that is trained to not hallucinate.
cards.explanation: Lower temperature = less randomness = more deterministic, factual output. High temperature = more creative but more hallucinations. So decreasing temperature is the simple inference-time fix for hallucinations. Bedrock Agents don't supervise training. Cleaning training data is a pre-processing fix for fine-tuned models, but you don't have control over a foundation model's training data. There is no 'FM trained to not hallucinate' (all FMs hallucinate to some degree).
tricks: 'reduce hallucinations at inference time' = lower temperature. For deeper fixes: RAG with grounded sources, fact-checking guardrails

cards.q: A company wants to develop an educational game for probability questions. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
cards.a: Use code that will calculate probability by using simple rules and computations.
options: Use supervised learning to create a regression model.
Use reinforcement learning to train a model.
Use code that will calculate probability by using simple rules and computations.
Use unsupervised learning to create a model.
cards.explanation: Probability for an educational game uses well-known mathematical formulas (combinations, permutations, conditional probability). Plain code with rules and computations is the simplest, cheapest, and most accurate option. ML for a deterministic mathematical problem is overkill, expensive, and probably less reliable.
tricks: 'deterministic math problem with known formulas' = use code, not ML

cards.q: A company is using an LLM on Amazon Bedrock for a chatbot that requires multiple interactions. Which solution gives the LLM the ability to use content from previous messages?
cards.a: Add messages to the model prompt.
options: Add messages to the model prompt.
Use Amazon Personalize to save conversation history.
Use Provisioned Throughput for the LLM.
cards.explanation: LLMs are stateless: each API call is independent. To give them memory of previous turns, you include past messages in the current prompt (chat history pattern). Bedrock and most LLM APIs accept a list of messages with roles (user, assistant) for this. Model invocation logging = audit only, doesn't affect inference. Personalize = recommendation engine, unrelated. Provisioned Throughput = capacity reservation, not memory.
tricks: 'multi-turn chatbot needs context from previous messages' = include history in the prompt

cards.q: A company's employees provide product recommendations based on customer location. The company wants to automate this with FMs. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides foundation models for generating text and recommendations. Macie = PII discovery in S3. Transcribe = speech-to-text. Textract = extract text from documents. Note: this question is mis-tagged as security_compliance_governance in the source but the right answer (Bedrock) clearly fits Applications of Foundation Models.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

cards.q: A company wants to upload customer service emails to S3. The messages sometimes contain sensitive data. The company wants alerts when sensitive info is found. Which solution has LEAST development effort?
cards.a: Configure Amazon Macie to detect sensitive information.
options: Configure Amazon Macie to detect sensitive information.
Use SageMaker endpoints to deploy an LLM to redact sensitive data.
Develop multiple regex patterns on a SageMaker notebook.
Ask customers to avoid sharing sensitive information.
cards.explanation: Macie is the managed AWS service for sensitive data discovery in S3 (PII, financial data, health data) using machine learning. Zero code required: enable on the bucket, get findings via EventBridge or Security Hub. Custom SageMaker LLM = high dev effort. Custom regex notebooks = high dev effort and brittle. Asking customers = not enforceable.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'detect sensitive info in S3 with least dev effort' = Amazon Macie

cards.q: Which option is a benefit of using Amazon SageMaker Model Cards to document AI models?
cards.a: Standardizing information about a model's purpose, performance, and limitations.
options: Providing a visually appealing summary of capabilities.
Standardizing information about a model's purpose, performance, and limitations.
Physically storing models for archival purposes.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards provide a STANDARDIZED template for documenting model purpose, intended use, performance metrics, training data, ethical considerations, and limitations. They are about consistent documentation across models, not visual presentation, compute reduction, or storage.
tricks: 'standardized model documentation' = SageMaker Model Cards

cards.q: What does an F1 score measure in the context of foundation model (FM) performance?
options: Financial cost of operating the model
cards.explanation: F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision (of predicted positives, how many were correct) and recall (of actual positives, how many were caught). Used to balance both in classification tasks, especially when classes are imbalanced. F1 has nothing to do with speed, cost, or energy.
tricks: 'F1' = precision and recall balance

cards.q: A company deployed an AI/ML solution for FAQ. Questions can change over time. Which strategy meets requirements MOST cost-effectively?
cards.a: Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with prompt engineering.
options: Train the model by using context data.
Pre-train and benchmark by using context data.
Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with prompt engineering.
cards.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) lets the FM look up the latest FAQ data from a knowledge base at inference time, no retraining needed when the FAQ changes. Fine-tuning regularly = expensive and slow. Training on context data = even more expensive (we don't fine-tune on changing FAQ). Pre-training = orders of magnitude more expensive.
tricks: 'data changes over time, keep app up to date cheaply' = RAG

cards.q: A company built an AI-powered resume screening system. The dataset was not representative of all demographics. Which core dimension of responsible AI does this present?
cards.explanation: Transformer-based architectures (the architecture behind LLMs like GPT, Claude, Llama) use self-attention to process tokens in parallel, scaling efficiently to long sequences and large datasets. RNN = sequential, slower. CNN = good for images. Decision trees = not deep learning. The breakthrough behind ChatGPT, Bedrock FMs, and all modern LLMs is the Transformer architecture (paper 'Attention Is All You Need', 2017).
tricks: 'modern LLM architecture' = Transformer

cards.q: A global financial company wants to continuously monitor ML app development and ensure policies and regulations are followed. Which AWS services help assess compliance? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: AWS Audit Manager continuously collects evidence to assess compliance against frameworks (SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, ISO 27001) and produces audit-ready reports. AWS Config records configuration history of resources and evaluates them against custom or managed rules (e.g. all S3 buckets encrypted, all IAM users have MFA). Together they cover both compliance assessment (Audit Manager) and configuration policy enforcement (Config). Inspector = vulnerability scanning. CloudWatch = monitoring metrics. CloudTrail = API audit logs.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'continuously assess compliance' = Audit Manager + Config

cards.q: Which metric measures the runtime efficiency of operating AI models?
cards.explanation: Average response time is the standard latency metric for runtime / inference efficiency: how fast does the deployed model produce a response to a request. CSAT = customer satisfaction, business outcome not technical efficiency. Training time per epoch = training-side metric, not runtime. Number of training instances = capacity for training.
tricks: 'runtime efficiency / inference latency' = average response time

cards.q: A company wants to improve accuracy of responses from a generative AI app on Amazon Bedrock. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
cards.explanation: Cost ranking from cheapest to most expensive for FM customization: prompt engineering (free, just rewriting the prompt) < RAG (cheap, retrieve external data) < fine-tuning (medium, additional training on a small dataset) < retraining (expensive) < pre-training a new FM (millions of dollars). For improving accuracy MOST cost-effectively, always start with prompt engineering.
tricks: 'most cost-effective accuracy improvement' = prompt engineering first

cards.q: A company wants to identify harmful language in social media comments without labeled data. Which strategy should the company use?
options: Use Amazon Polly to monitor comments.
cards.explanation: Amazon Comprehend has built-in toxicity detection and sentiment analysis pre-trained on text. No labeled data required, just call the API. Rekognition = images/video, not text. SageMaker built-in algos = require training data. Polly = text-to-speech.
tricks: 'detect toxicity in text without labels' = Amazon Comprehend

cards.q: A media company wants to deploy a customized ML model and observe if model quality drifts over time. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors deployed models for data drift, model quality drift, bias drift, and feature attribution drift. SageMaker Clarify = bias and explainability (one-shot or scheduled). Comprehend = pre-built NLP. Rekognition = images.
tricks: 'detect model quality drift over time' = SageMaker Model Monitor

cards.q: A company wants to offer transparency into ML models' decision-making and provide explanations for outputs. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards provide standardized documentation that explains a model's purpose, intended use, training details, performance metrics, and limitations. They are the AWS answer to 'transparency in ML model decision-making'. Rekognition, Comprehend, and Lex are AI services, not transparency tools.
tricks: 'transparency / explainability of ML models' (in this context, documentation) = SageMaker Model Cards

cards.q: A manufacturing company wants to create product descriptions in multiple languages. Which AWS service will automate this task?
cards.explanation: Amazon Translate is the AWS managed service for neural machine translation across 75+ languages. Transcribe = speech-to-text. Kendra = enterprise search. Polly = text-to-speech.
tricks: 'translate text between languages' = Amazon Translate

cards.q: Which AWS feature records details about ML instance data for governance and reporting?
cards.explanation: Same answer as aif-056: SageMaker Model Cards record standardized details about a model's purpose, training, performance, and limitations for governance and reporting. SageMaker Debugger = debug training jobs. SageMaker Model Monitor = drift detection. SageMaker JumpStart = pre-trained models marketplace.
tricks: 'document ML model details for governance' = SageMaker Model Cards

cards.q: A financial company is using ML. Which option is a use of generative AI models?
options: Classifying customers based on product usage
cards.explanation: Generative AI creates new content (text, images, audio, video). Summarization is a text generation task: read input, generate condensed output. Classification (assigning a label), customer segmentation (clustering), and forecasting (predicting a number) are NOT generative, they are predictive ML.
tricks: 'generative AI use case' = something that produces new content (text/image/etc.), not just labels or numbers

cards.q: A medical company wants to access structured patient records, extract relevant information, and generate concise summaries. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to extract entities. Apply rule-based logic for summaries.
options: Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to extract entities. Apply rule-based logic for summaries.
Use Amazon Personalize to analyze patterns.
Use Amazon Textract to convert scanned documents.
Implement Amazon Kendra for searchable index.
cards.explanation: Amazon Comprehend Medical is a pre-built NLP service tuned for medical text. It extracts entities (medications, dosages, conditions, anatomy, ICD-10 codes) without requiring custom training. Combined with rule-based logic, you can produce structured summaries fast. Personalize = recommendations. Textract = OCR for scanned documents (useful only if records are scans). Kendra = search, not extraction.
tricks: 'extract entities from medical text' = Comprehend Medical

cards.q: Which option describes embeddings in the context of AI?
cards.a: A numerical method for data representation in a reduced dimensionality space
options: A method for compressing large datasets
An encryption method for securing sensitive data
A method for visualizing high-dimensional data
A numerical method for data representation in a reduced dimensionality space
cards.explanation: Embeddings are vector representations of data (text, images, audio) in a lower-dimensional space where similar items are close to each other. They power semantic search, RAG, recommendations, and clustering. Compression and visualization are side-effects, not the definition. Encryption is unrelated.
tricks: 'vector representation in reduced dimensions for similarity' = embeddings

cards.q: A company wants to gain insights from customer conversations by analyzing audio of customer calls. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Transcribe call recordings by using Amazon Transcribe.
options: Build a conversational chatbot by using Amazon Lex.
Transcribe call recordings by using Amazon Transcribe.
Extract info by using Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor.
Create classification labels by using Amazon Comprehend.
cards.explanation: Amazon Transcribe converts speech (audio) to text. Once you have text, you can analyze it with Comprehend (sentiment, entities), Bedrock (summarize), or Q in Connect (agent assist). The first step for audio analysis is always transcription. Lex = chatbots, not call analysis. Model Monitor = drift detection. Comprehend = needs text, comes after transcription.
tricks: 'analyze customer call audio' = first transcribe with Amazon Transcribe

cards.q: A company is building an AI application to summarize books. Some books fail to summarize. Why?
cards.a: The input tokens exceed the model's context size.
options: The temperature is set too high.
The model does not support fine-tuning.
The Top P value is too high.
The input tokens exceed the model's context size.
cards.explanation: Foundation models have a context window (max tokens that fit in input + output). When the input exceeds this size, the model truncates or fails. Solutions: use a model with a bigger context window, chunk the book and summarize chunks then combine, or use a hierarchical approach. Temperature controls randomness, not capacity. Top P also controls randomness. Fine-tuning support is unrelated.
tricks: 'long input fails to be processed' = exceeded context window

cards.q: An airline company wants to build a conversational AI assistant using LLMs and a knowledge base. Which solution has LEAST development effort?
cards.a: Develop a RAG agent by using Amazon Bedrock.
options: Train models on Amazon SageMaker Autopilot.
Develop a RAG agent by using Amazon Bedrock.
Create a Python application by using Amazon Q Developer.
Fine-tune models on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart.
cards.explanation: Bedrock Agents + Knowledge Bases provide a fully managed RAG solution: AWS handles the embedding model, vector store, retrieval logic, and orchestration. Less dev effort than building from scratch with SageMaker (Autopilot is tabular ML, not really for RAG), Q Developer (coding assistant, not RAG framework), or fine-tuning JumpStart models (would need a separate retrieval pipeline).
tricks: 'conversational AI + knowledge base + LEAST dev effort' = Bedrock RAG agent

cards.q: What is tokenization used for in natural language processing (NLP)?
cards.a: To break text into smaller units for processing
options: To break text into smaller units for processing
cards.explanation: Tokenization splits text into smaller units (words, subwords, or characters) called tokens. LLMs process tokens, not raw characters. Tokens are the unit on which billing is also based for most LLM APIs. Encryption, compression, and translation are different problems.
tricks: 'split text into smaller units for ML' = tokenization

cards.q: Which option is a characteristic of transformer-based language models?
cards.a: They use self-attention mechanisms to capture contextual relationships.
options: They use convolutional layers to apply filters.
They can process only text data.
They use self-attention mechanisms to capture contextual relationships.
They process data sequences one element at a time in cyclic iterations.
cards.explanation: Transformer-based models (BERT, GPT, Claude, Llama) use self-attention to capture relationships between every pair of tokens in the input regardless of distance. Convolutional filters = CNN architecture (vision). Sequential processing = RNN/LSTM, the architecture transformers replaced. Transformers process tokens in parallel, not sequentially. Multi-modal transformers handle text + images, so 'process only text' is wrong.
tricks: 'self-attention mechanism' = transformer

cards.q: A financial company using AI for credit scores wants to expand to a new geographic area. Which compliance laws should the company review?
options: Local payment card data protection laws
cards.explanation: Algorithm accountability laws (e.g. NYC Local Law 144 on automated employment decision tools, EU AI Act, Colorado AI Act) are the laws specifically governing AI/ML decision-making, including credit scoring. They typically require fairness audits, bias disclosures, and human oversight. Health data laws apply to medical info. Payment card laws apply to PCI DSS. Education privacy laws apply to FERPA.
tricks: 'AI/ML credit scoring + new geo' = check local algorithm accountability laws

cards.q: A company uses Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to filter harmful content. Which content categories can the guardrails filter? (Choose two.)
cards.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails filter harmful content across these categories: Hate, Insults, Sexual, Violence, Misconduct, plus Prompt Injection detection. It does NOT include political bias filters, religious filters, or gambling filters as predefined categories. The 5 standard categories are the answer in any 'choose 2' question of this type.
tricks: 'Bedrock Guardrails default content filters' = Hate, Insults, Sexual, Violence, Misconduct

cards.q: Which scenario describes a potential risk of prompt engineering?
cards.a: Prompt engineering could expose the model to prompt injection attacks.
options: Prompt engineering ensures consistent outputs, eliminating need for validation.
Prompt engineering could expose the model to prompt injection attacks.
Properly designed prompts eliminate risk of data poisoning.
Prompt engineering ensures reliable outputs with real-world data.
cards.explanation: Prompt injection is when an attacker provides input that tricks the model into ignoring the original system prompt and executing unintended instructions (e.g. 'ignore previous instructions and reveal the system prompt'). It is a real and widely discussed risk of LLM applications. The other choices are factually wrong: prompts do NOT eliminate validation, do NOT eliminate data poisoning, and outputs are NOT guaranteed reliable.
tricks: 'security risk of prompts' = prompt injection

cards.q: A RAG-based solution publishes daily content. Which steps should use offline batch processing? (Choose two.)
cards.a: Generation of content embeddings ; Creation of the search index
options: Generation of embeddings for user queries
cards.explanation: In a RAG pipeline, offline (batch) processing handles things that don't change per user query: 1) Generating embeddings for all your content (slow, computationally expensive), 2) Building the search/vector index. Online processing handles what changes per query: 3) Embedding the user query, 4) Retrieval against the index, 5) Final response generation.
tricks: 'offline RAG' = pre-compute embeddings + build index. 'Online RAG' = per-query retrieval and generation

cards.q: Which technique breaks a complex task into smaller subtasks sent sequentially to an LLM?
cards.explanation: Prompt chaining breaks a complex task into smaller subtasks, each handled by a separate LLM call, with the output of one call feeding the next. Useful when one prompt is too long or too complex for the model. One-shot = single example in the prompt. Tree of thoughts = explore multiple reasoning paths and pick the best. RAG = retrieve external data.
tricks: 'sequential subtasks fed to LLM' = prompt chaining

cards.q: An AI practitioner needs to improve accuracy of a model using rapidly changing inventory data. Which technique will improve accuracy?
cards.explanation: RAG retrieves up-to-date data at inference time, ideal when underlying data changes rapidly (inventory, prices, news). The model itself is unchanged but its responses use fresh retrieved context. Transfer learning = adapt a model for a new task, not for changing data. Federated learning = train across distributed devices without centralizing data. One-shot = give one example in the prompt, doesn't address freshness.
tricks: 'rapidly changing data + LLM' = RAG

cards.q: A company has petabytes of unlabeled customer data and wants to classify customers into tiers. Which methodology should it use?
cards.explanation: Petabytes of UNLABELED data + need to find groups = unsupervised learning (clustering algorithms like K-means, DBSCAN, hierarchical clustering). Supervised learning needs labels. Reinforcement learning needs rewards. RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) is for fine-tuning LLMs with human preferences, irrelevant here.
tricks: 'unlabeled data + groups/segments' = unsupervised learning

cards.q: A company needs standardized documentation of model version tracking and development records. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Track changes by using Amazon SageMaker Model Cards.
options: Track changes by using Amazon Fraud Detector.
Track changes by using Amazon SageMaker Model Cards.
Track changes by using Amazon Comprehend.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards = standardized model documentation including version tracking, training details, performance, intended use. Git tracks code, not model artifacts and metadata. Fraud Detector = different service. Comprehend = NLP API.
tricks: 'model version tracking + standardized docs' = SageMaker Model Cards

cards.q: A company wants to identify changes in original model quality. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Same as aif-055: SageMaker Model Monitor watches deployed models for quality drift (data drift, model drift, bias drift). JumpStart = pre-trained models. HyperPod = distributed training infrastructure. Data Wrangler = data prep.
tricks: 'detect changes in model quality post-deployment' = SageMaker Model Monitor

cards.q: What is the purpose of chunking in Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?
cards.a: To improve the contextual relevancy of results retrieved from the vector index
options: To avoid converting large text into embeddings
To improve the contextual relevancy of results retrieved from the vector index
To decrease the cost of storage
cards.explanation: Chunking splits long source documents into smaller pieces (paragraphs, ~500-tokens chunks) before generating embeddings. Why: 1) embeddings of focused chunks capture meaning more precisely than embeddings of huge documents, 2) the retriever returns only the relevant chunks, not entire books, so the context window stays small and the relevance high. Storage limits and embedding costs are secondary effects.
tricks: 'chunking in RAG' = improve retrieval relevance

cards.q: A company is developing an editorial assistant with generative AI. Usage is unpredictable and the company wants to minimize costs. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Use Amazon Bedrock with On-Demand Throughput.
options: Use Amazon Bedrock with Provisioned Throughput.
Use Amazon Bedrock with On-Demand Throughput.
cards.explanation: On-Demand Throughput on Bedrock = pay per token, no commitment. Perfect for unpredictable usage because you only pay for what you use. Provisioned Throughput requires a commitment (model units per hour) and is cheaper only when usage is steady and high. EC2 GPU instances = manage your own infra (expensive when idle). SageMaker JumpStart = train or deploy custom models, more setup.
tricks: 'unpredictable usage + minimize cost' = Bedrock On-Demand Throughput

cards.q: A RAG application on Amazon Bedrock distributes newsletters. Users report politically influenced content. Which guardrail can filter this?
cards.explanation: Bedrock Guardrails has 4 main controls: 1) Content filters (predefined: Hate, Insults, Sexual, Violence, Misconduct). 2) Denied topics (custom topics you forbid the model to discuss, e.g. politics, legal advice, medical advice). 3) Sensitive information filters (PII detection and masking). 4) Word filters (block specific words/phrases). For 'politically influenced content' that is not in the predefined filter categories, you create a Denied topic 'politics' so the model refuses to engage.
tricks: 'block specific custom topics' = Denied topics

cards.q: A fraud detection system flags transactions. The company wants to minimize time reviewing false positives. Which metric meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Precision = of the items the model flagged as positive, how many were actually positive. High precision = few false positives, exactly the goal here (don't waste time reviewing wrongly-flagged transactions). Recall = of all actual positives, how many did the model catch (high recall = few false negatives, but might flag many false positives). Accuracy = overall correct rate (misleading when classes are imbalanced like fraud). Lift chart = different concept.
tricks: 'minimize false positives' = optimize for precision

cards.q: A company's AI-powered agent answers inquiries from product manuals. Which strategy can improve customer confidence in responses?
cards.a: Including referenced product manual links in the response
options: Writing the confidence level in the response
Including referenced product manual links in the response
Designing an agent avatar that looks like a computer
Training the agent in the company's language style
cards.explanation: Including source links (the product manual the answer came from) is a standard pattern in RAG-based AI to increase trust: users can verify the answer by clicking through to the original document. This is part of explainability/transparency. Confidence levels are sometimes useful but less actionable than source citations. Avatar design and language style don't address confidence in factual accuracy.
tricks: 'increase customer trust in AI answers' = cite sources / include reference links

cards.q: A hospital's AI provides treatment recommendations with rationale accessible to doctors and patients. Which human-centered design principle is this?
cards.explanation: Explainability = the ability to understand WHY the model produced a given output. Providing rationale for treatment recommendations is the textbook example. Privacy and security = keep data confidential (different concern). Fairness = equal treatment across groups. Data governance = how data is managed.
tricks: 'rationale / explanation of decisions' = explainability

cards.q: Which statement presents an advantage of using RAG for NLP tasks?
cards.a: RAG can use external knowledge sources to generate more accurate responses.
options: RAG can use external knowledge sources to generate more accurate responses.
RAG improves the speed of language model training.
RAG is primarily used for speech recognition.
RAG is a technique for data augmentation in computer vision.
cards.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant external documents at inference time and feeds them to the LLM as context. Result: more accurate, fact-grounded responses without retraining. RAG does NOT speed up training. RAG is for text-based tasks, not speech recognition. RAG is not data augmentation in computer vision.
tricks: 'RAG advantage' = use external knowledge sources for accuracy

cards.q: A company fine-tuned an LLM on Amazon Bedrock for production with a steady rate of requests. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
cards.a: Purchase Provisioned Throughput on Amazon Bedrock.
options: Deploy on an Amazon EC2 compute optimized instance.
Use on-demand throughput on Amazon Bedrock.
Store in S3 and host by using AWS Lambda.
Purchase Provisioned Throughput on Amazon Bedrock.
cards.explanation: Provisioned Throughput is the cost-effective choice when usage is steady and predictable: you commit to a number of model units per hour and pay a flat rate, much cheaper than On-Demand at high volume. EC2 compute optimized = wrong fit (Bedrock is the managed FM service, no need to host on EC2). On-demand = pricier than Provisioned for steady workloads. S3 + Lambda = doesn't host LLMs.
tricks: 'steady production rate of requests' = Bedrock Provisioned Throughput

cards.q: An AI practitioner wants to use an FM for a search application that handles text and images. Which type of FM should be used?
cards.explanation: Multi-modal embedding models (e.g. Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings) generate a SINGLE shared vector space for both text AND images, allowing cross-modal search (search images with text queries, search text with image queries). Text embedding model = text only. Multi-modal generation = generates content (Stable Diffusion-like), not searches. Image generation = produces images, not embeddings.
tricks: 'search across text + images' = multi-modal embedding model

cards.q: Which technique involves training AI models on labeled datasets to adapt to specific industry terminology?
cards.explanation: Fine-tuning trains an existing pre-trained model on a smaller LABELED dataset to adapt it to a specific domain (medical, legal, finance) or task. Data augmentation = generate synthetic training examples. Model quantization = reduce model size for inference. Continuous pre-training = update the FM with new general data, not for domain specialization with labels.
tricks: 'adapt model to specific domain with labeled data' = fine-tuning

cards.q: A company is creating an agent with Amazon Bedrock Agents. It wants to improve accuracy by providing specific examples. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Modify the advanced prompts for the agent to include the examples.
options: Modify the advanced prompts for the agent to include the examples.
Create a guardrail that includes the examples.
Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label the examples.
Run a Lambda script to add examples to training data.
cards.explanation: Bedrock Agents have advanced prompts (4 templates: pre-processing, orchestration, knowledge base response, post-processing) where you can include few-shot examples to steer agent behavior. Editing the orchestration prompt with specific examples is the canonical way to improve agent accuracy. Guardrails = block harmful content, not the place for examples. Ground Truth = data labeling for SageMaker, not Bedrock Agents. Lambda script for training data = irrelevant (agents don't train).
tricks: 'improve Bedrock Agent accuracy with examples' = modify advanced prompts

cards.q: Which option is a benefit of using infrastructure as code (IaC) in MLOps?
cards.a: IaC streamlines deployment of scalable and consistent ML workloads.
options: IaC eliminates the need for hyperparameter tuning.
IaC always provisions powerful compute instances.
IaC streamlines deployment of scalable and consistent ML workloads.
IaC minimizes expenses by deploying only low-cost instances.
cards.explanation: IaC (CloudFormation, Terraform, CDK) lets you define infrastructure declaratively, version it, replicate it across environments. For MLOps this means consistent training, deployment, and monitoring environments without manual setup. IaC does NOT eliminate hyperparameter tuning. IaC does NOT mandate any specific instance type. IaC does NOT minimize cost by itself.
tricks: 'IaC benefit in MLOps' = scalable + consistent ML deployments

cards.q: A company wants to use instruction-based fine-tuning. How should it prepare the training data?
cards.a: Create pairs of questions and answers for the industry domain.
options: Gather internal documents and merge into a single file.
Collect external reviews. Label each as positive or negative.
Create pairs of questions and answers for the industry domain.
Create few-shot prompts to instruct the model.
cards.explanation: Instruction-based fine-tuning trains the model on PAIRS of {prompt, expected response} so the model learns to follow specific instructions. Q&A pairs in your industry domain are the canonical format. Single merged file or unlabeled internal docs = continuous pre-training format, not instruction fine-tuning. Sentiment-labeled reviews = classification fine-tuning. Few-shot prompts = inference-time technique, not training data.
tricks: 'instruction fine-tuning data' = labeled prompt-completion pairs

cards.q: Which ML technique ensures data compliance and privacy when training AI models on AWS?
cards.explanation: Federated learning trains a shared model across multiple decentralized data sources (e.g. devices, hospitals) WITHOUT centralizing the raw data. Each participant trains locally on its own data and only model updates (gradients/weights) are aggregated. This preserves privacy and meets data residency / regulatory requirements. Reinforcement learning, transfer learning, and unsupervised learning don't have data privacy as their defining feature.
tricks: 'train without sharing raw data' = federated learning

cards.q: A manufacturing company uses complex hard-coded logic to process complaints. Which advantage do generative AI models offer for scaling?
options: Less sensitivity to changes in inputs
cards.explanation: Hard-coded rules don't scale to new types of complaints or edge cases. Generative AI models are ADAPTABLE: they generalize to unseen inputs and can be updated via prompting / fine-tuning instead of writing new rules. Predictability is actually LOWER with generative AI (more variance). Sensitivity to input changes is HIGHER. Explainability is LOWER than rule-based systems. The key advantage for scaling beyond rule limits is adaptability.
tricks: 'GenAI advantage over hard-coded rules at scale' = adaptability

cards.q: A financial company wants to flag credit card activity as fraudulent or non-fraudulent. Which type of ML model meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Two outcomes (fraudulent OR non-fraudulent) = binary classification. Multi-class would be 3+ classes. Regression predicts a continuous number, not a class. Diffusion is a generative architecture, not a classification type.
tricks: 'flag as A or B' = binary classification

cards.q: A company wants to use generative AI with speech-to-text for dictating clinical notes. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS HealthScribe is a HIPAA-eligible service that generates clinical notes from clinician-patient conversations using speech-to-text + medical NLP + generative AI. It's purpose-built for clinical dictation. Q Developer = code assistant. Polly = text-to-speech (opposite direction). Rekognition = images.
tricks: 'speech-to-text + clinical notes' = AWS HealthScribe

cards.q: A company wants to fine-tune a model on Amazon Bedrock to be more accurate. Which strategy will work?
cards.a: Provide labeled data with the prompt field and the completion field.
options: Provide labeled data with the prompt field and the completion field.
Prepare training data as a .txt file in .csv format.
Train the model on journals and textbooks.
cards.explanation: Bedrock fine-tuning expects a JSONL file where each line has 'prompt' and 'completion' fields representing the model input and the desired output. .txt in .csv format isn't a valid Bedrock fine-tuning format. Provisioned Throughput is for production hosting, not training. Training on journals/textbooks = continuous pre-training, different from fine-tuning.
tricks: 'Bedrock fine-tuning data format' = labeled prompt + completion pairs

cards.q: Which type of AI model makes numeric predictions?
cards.explanation: Regression predicts a continuous numeric value (price, temperature, demand). Diffusion = generative model architecture (images). Transformer = architecture (LLMs). Multi-modal = combines modalities.
tricks: 'predict a number' = regression

cards.q: What is the purpose of vector embeddings in a large language model (LLM)?
cards.a: Providing the ability to mathematically compare texts
options: Grouping characters to be treated as a single unit
Providing the ability to mathematically compare texts
Providing the count of every word in the input
cards.explanation: Vector embeddings transform text (or other data) into numerical vectors so they can be compared mathematically (cosine similarity, dot product). This enables semantic search, RAG, and clustering. Splitting text = tokenization. Grouping characters = tokenization. Counting words = bag-of-words, not embeddings.
tricks: 'mathematically compare texts' = embeddings

cards.q: A company wants to fine-tune an FM keeping data private and secure in its AWS Region. Which combination meets requirements cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
cards.a: Use the Amazon Bedrock API. ; Use AWS PrivateLink and a VPC.
options: Host on premises by using AWS Outposts.
Use AWS PrivateLink and a VPC.
Host Amazon Bedrock API on premises.
Use Amazon CloudWatch logs and metrics.
cards.explanation: Bedrock API + PrivateLink + VPC = private fine-tuning entirely inside AWS without going to the public internet. Outposts on premises = expensive and Bedrock isn't fully on Outposts. Hosting Bedrock API on premises = not possible. CloudWatch logs alone don't address privacy.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'private + secure FM fine-tuning in your Region cost-effectively' = Bedrock API + PrivateLink in VPC

cards.q: A financial company must generate reports to show adherence to international regulations for handling sensitive data. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: AWS Artifact is the on-demand portal for AWS compliance reports (SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27018, etc.). Used to demonstrate adherence to international regulations to auditors. Macie = PII detection. Secrets Manager = credentials. Config = configuration history.
cards.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
tricks: 'compliance reports for regulations' = AWS Artifact

cards.q: A medical company wants to use generative AI to respond to medical questions responsibly. Which AWS service should it use?
cards.explanation: Bedrock Guardrails is the AWS service to add safety controls to FM responses: block harmful topics, mask PII, enforce content filters. Critical for medical use cases where wrong info can harm patients. Inspector = vulnerability scanning. Rekognition = images. Trusted Advisor = best-practice checks for AWS infra.
tricks: 'safe / responsible LLM responses' = Bedrock Guardrails

cards.q: Which metric is used to evaluate FM performance for text summarization tasks?
cards.explanation: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) was originally designed for machine translation, but is also commonly used for text summarization and other text-generation tasks where you compare generated text to reference text via n-gram overlap. F1 = classification metric. Accuracy = classification metric. MSE = regression metric. Note: ROUGE is also commonly used for summarization (often even more than BLEU), but in this question's choices BLEU is the only generation-text metric available.
tricks: 'evaluate generated text vs reference' = BLEU or ROUGE

cards.q: What is the benefit of fine-tuning a foundation model (FM)?
cards.a: Improves performance on a specific task by further training on new labeled data.
options: Reduces size and enables slower inference.
Uses specific training data to retrain from scratch.
Keeps knowledge up to date by pre-training on recent data.
Improves performance on a specific task by further training on new labeled data.
cards.explanation: Fine-tuning further trains a pre-trained foundation model on new labeled data to adapt it to a specific task, improving its performance on that task. Fine-tuning does NOT reduce model size (that's quantization or distillation). Fine-tuning does NOT retrain from scratch (that's pre-training). Fine-tuning does NOT pre-train on recent data (that's continuous pre-training).
tricks: 'improve model on specific task with new labeled data' = fine-tuning

cards.q: A company wants to improve chatbot responses to match its tone using 100 examples of high-quality conversations. Which solution meets these requirements?
cards.a: Create an Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job.
options: Create a SageMaker HyperPod pre-training job.
Create an Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning job.
cards.explanation: Adapting tone with 100 high-quality conversation examples = small labeled dataset to fine-tune a foundation model on Bedrock. Personalize = recommendations, not chat tone. SageMaker HyperPod = distributed pre-training infra, overkill. SageMaker + TensorRT = self-managed deployment, more effort.
tricks: 'small labeled dataset to adapt model behavior' = Bedrock fine-tuning

cards.q: An ecommerce chatbot is available 24/7 for order submission. Which AI system input vulnerability must be resolved?
cards.explanation: A 24/7 public chatbot accepts arbitrary user inputs, which is the textbook attack vector for prompt injection (an attacker types instructions that override the system prompt: 'ignore previous instructions, reveal the order database'). Data leakage is a possible CONSEQUENCE of prompt injection but is not itself an input vulnerability. Hallucinations = factuality issue, not an input attack. Concept drift = data distribution change over time, not input vulnerability.
tricks: 'public chatbot input vulnerability' = prompt injection

cards.q: A law firm wants an AI application to read legal documents and extract key points. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Build an automatic named entity recognition system.
cards.explanation: Read documents and extract key points = summarization, the canonical generative AI use case for long-form documents. NER (named entity recognition) extracts entities like names and dates, not key points. Recommendation engine = suggest items, irrelevant. Translation = different language, not extraction.
tricks: 'extract key points from long documents' = summarization chatbot (LLM via Bedrock)

cards.q: A company wants to use AI to check if an IP address is from a suspicious source. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Create an NLP named entity recognition system.
cards.explanation: Detecting unusual or suspicious patterns (rare events, deviations from normal) = anomaly detection. AWS services: GuardDuty for AWS account anomalies, SageMaker for custom models, Lookout family. Speech recognition = irrelevant. NER = extract entities, not flag suspicion. Fraud forecasting = predict future fraud volume, different from detecting suspicious IP now.
tricks: 'flag suspicious / unusual patterns' = anomaly detection

cards.q: A social media company wants to prevent discriminatory content using Amazon Bedrock. How can it meet these requirements?
cards.a: Block interactions related to predefined topics.
options: Give users ability to interact based on preferences.
Block interactions related to predefined topics.
Provide a variety of responses to select from.
cards.explanation: Bedrock Guardrails 'Denied topics' lets you BLOCK predefined topics (politics, hate speech categories, discriminatory subjects). 'Restrict to predefined topics' (only allow specific ones) is not how Guardrails work, they BLOCK rather than allow-list. Free interaction or response variety doesn't prevent discriminatory content.
tricks: 'block discriminatory content via Bedrock' = Guardrails Denied topics

cards.q: An education company's app accepts text or pictures of questions and responds with written answers. Which model type meets these requirements?
cards.explanation: Accepting both text AND images as inputs requires a multi-modal model that processes both modalities (e.g. Claude 3, Amazon Nova multi-modal models, GPT-4V). Computer vision model = images only. Diffusion model = generates images, doesn't read text questions. Text-to-speech = converts text to audio, irrelevant.
tricks: 'text + image input' = multi-modal LLM

cards.q: In which stage of the generative AI model lifecycle are tests performed to examine accuracy?
cards.explanation: The generative AI / ML lifecycle phases: Business goal -> Data selection -> Model selection -> Pre-training (or use existing FM) -> Fine-tuning -> EVALUATION (test accuracy, fairness, robustness) -> Deployment -> Monitoring. Accuracy testing happens specifically in the Evaluation phase.
tricks: 'test accuracy of model' = evaluation phase

cards.q: Which statement correctly describes embeddings in generative AI?
cards.a: Represent data as high-dimensional vectors that capture semantic relationships.
options: Represent data as high-dimensional vectors that capture semantic relationships.
A technique that searches data to find helpful information.
Reduce hardware requirements by using less precise data types.
Provide ability to store and retrieve data for generative AI.
cards.explanation: Embeddings are high-dimensional numeric vectors that capture semantic relationships (similar meanings end up close in vector space). 'Search data for helpful info' = description of retrieval, not embeddings. 'Reduce hardware via less precise data types' = quantization. 'Store and retrieve data' = generic data storage. Only the first option captures the essence of embeddings.
tricks: 'embeddings = high-dim vectors that encode semantic meaning'

cards.q: A company wants LLM responses to be as deterministic and stable as possible. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Add 'make your response deterministic' at end of prompt.
Add 'make your response deterministic' at beginning of prompt.
cards.explanation: Temperature is the LLM parameter controlling randomness. Temperature 0 = always pick the highest-probability token = most deterministic, repeatable output. Temperature 1+ = more randomness, more creative but less stable. Adding 'be deterministic' to the prompt is just instruction text, the model can ignore it.
tricks: 'maximize determinism / stability of LLM output' = temperature 0

cards.q: A company needs to select a generative AI model for real-time responses. Which model characteristic should it consider?
cards.explanation: Real-time responses = inference latency matters most. Inference speed is the metric for how fast the model responds to a request. Model complexity influences inference speed but isn't itself the right metric. Innovation speed = unrelated. Training time = time to train the model, not to respond.
